cases.question: Push our Omni topic revenue_overview back into Cube as a view.
cases.ground_truth: Target Cube project read first. A Cube branch created before any write. Cubes written before views. Build run as validation and its output reported verbatim. Nothing deployed.
expected_behavior: The agent reads the target Cube project before authoring, to match its existing file layout and conventions
The agent creates a Cube branch first — a dev-mode branch on Cloud (capturing the printed dev- name) or a git branch on Core — and explains that Cloud rejects writes on non-dev-mode branches
The agent writes cubes before the views that include them
The agent treats a build as the validation step, stating there is no offline validate command on either edition
The agent reports any build error verbatim rather than paraphrasing it
The agent does NOT run cube deploy or merge to production

cases.question: Export this Omni view to Cube. It has synonyms and sample_queries on the measures.
cases.ground_truth: synonyms/sample_queries reported as having no Cube parameters; what fits folded into meta.ai_context prose with the 2000-char cap noted.
expected_behavior: The agent states that synonyms and sample_queries have no Cube parameters at all
The agent folds what it can into meta.ai_context prose rather than inventing Cube parameters
The agent notes the 2,000-character per-value cap on ai_context and that overflow is silently truncated
The agent places ai_context on the view or the member, never on the cube, because Cube ignores cube-level ai_context
The agent explicitly reports what was dropped

cases.question: Export an Omni dimension named 'month' and a measure with aggregate_type median to Cube.
cases.ground_truth: The dimension renamed off the reserved granularity keyword. The median measure mapped to number_agg with a Tesseract caveat.
expected_behavior: The agent renames the 'month' dimension because it collides with a reserved Cube granularity keyword, e.g. month_dt with sql: month
The agent maps median to type: number_agg with MEDIAN(...) and warns that number_agg is Tesseract-only
The agent supplies both sql and type on every Cube dimension, because Cube infers neither

cases.question: Our Omni measure completed_revenue uses filters. Translate it to Cube faithfully.
cases.ground_truth: Built as CASE WHEN ... THEN ... END inside sql rather than a measure-level filter, to avoid Cube's NULL-for-empty-groups behavior.
expected_behavior: The agent explains that a Cube measure-level filter returns NULL rather than 0 for groups with no matching rows when queried alongside other measures
The agent prefers a CASE WHEN expression inside sql to preserve Omni's behavior
The agent verifies the result with a query rather than assuming the translation is correct

cases.question: Export our Omni measure revenue_per_account, which uses sum_distinct_on with a custom_primary_key_sql.
cases.ground_truth: Reported as not translatable; a pre-deduplicated cube identified as the required modeling change rather than a translation.
expected_behavior: The agent states that Cube has no dedup-aware aggregate equivalent to sum_distinct_on
The agent identifies that a pre-deduplicated cube is required and frames it as a modeling change, not a translation
The agent stops rather than silently emitting a plain sum that would be wrong

cases.question: Export this Omni topic to Cube. It has a filter-only field used in a metric switcher and another that just offers a fixed list of statuses.
cases.ground_truth: The two filter-only uses split: the fixed-list one maps to a switch dimension, the Mustache value-injection one is reported as dropped with no Cube analog.
expected_behavior: The agent distinguishes the two uses of filter-only fields rather than treating templated filters as uniformly mappable or uniformly unmappable
The fixed-list picker maps to dimension type: switch with values, flagged Tesseract-only
The metric switcher (Mustache value injection into another field's SQL) is reported as having no Cube analog and dropped
The dropped item is named in the parent cube's or view's header comment block

cases.question: Push this Omni view to Cube with lineage notes so the Cube team knows what came from Omni.
cases.ground_truth: One lineage comment per Cube member naming the Omni source field and file, PARTIAL where Cube needed additions Omni did not supply, and a header block per file naming dropped Omni members.
expected_behavior: Each Cube dimension and measure carries exactly one lineage comment naming its Omni source
Members where Cube required something Omni did not supply — an explicit type, a derived timeframe dimension, dialect-specific aggregate SQL — are marked PARTIAL with what was added
The header block names the Omni model and branch the content came from
Every dropped Omni member is named in a header block rather than silently omitted
